blocks.raw: <Callout>Reading the arc this way reveals a key insight: each layer presupposes the one before it. You cannot meaningfully discuss a philosophical position without grounding in the elements and principles that position was arguing about. You cannot apply space planning theory without understanding design perception. The sequence is a learning sequence, not just an organizational one.</Callout>

blocks.raw: <Note>Louis Kahn's distinction between "served spaces" (living rooms, offices, classrooms — the spaces people inhabit for primary activities) and "servant spaces" (corridors, mechanical rooms, toilets — the spaces that support served spaces) is both a Theory principle and a practical programming tool. It appears in Theory questions and Design exercises alike.</Note>

blocks.raw: <Tip>Study the PAGASA wind rose data for the Philippine archipelago alongside your tropical architecture notes. Knowing that northeast monsoon dominates November–February and southwest monsoon dominates June–September — and knowing that building orientation should favor cross-ventilation from the prevailing direction — gives you a design rationlea that is both theoretically grounded and locally specific.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <Warn>Integration questions are where students who memorized without understanding fall short. If you only know what Critical Regionalism is in the abstract, you cannot apply it to a specific Filipino climate and cultural context. Study each subtopic with an eye toward "how would I use this to make a design decision?"</Warn>
